newsitem.title: USA: Rain aids Iowa corn and soybeans, east still dry.
newsitem.headline: Rain aids Iowa corn and soybeans, east still dry.

text.p: Much-needed rain reached most of Iowa in the week ended Sunday, improving corn and soybean conditions, but some eastern areas remained dry, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.

"Areas of the east central and south central districts are still very dry," the report said. "Reporters are commenting that the corn and soybean progress is excellent, except on lighter soils or areas in need of moisture."
Corn was rated three percent poor, 17 percent fair, 58 percent good and 22 percent excellent. The crop was pollinating on 87 percent of the acreage.
Soybeans were rated three percent poor, 19 percent fair, 58 percent good and 20 percent excellent. Soybeans were blooming on 87 percent of the acreage, ahead of average pace.
As of Friday, topsoil moisture was rated eight percent very short, 26 percent short, 58 percent adequate and eight percent surplus.

Pasture was rated eight percent very poor, 17 percent poor, 38 percent fair, 33 percent good and four percent excellent. Pinkeye was reported in the southwest and south central districts. Flies were becoming a problem in some areas, the report said.
